scope: All five sprint plans read; Sprints 1-2 audited against code, gaps corrected, Sprint 3 implemented. Sprints 4-5 remain planned.

baseline.backendTestsResult: passed, but the curriculum suite expected the unauthenticated-by-assessment completion bypass
baseline.workingTree: Existing uncommitted auth, curriculum, server, seeder, terms-modal and partial quiz backend changes were present and incorporated.

conclusion.sprint1Before: Not fully implemented: consent, JWT configuration/profile, and demo seeding gaps.
conclusion.sprint2Before: Not fully implemented: critical quiz-free progression and content access bypass, missing guest access and formatted lecture rendering.
conclusion.sprint2After: Implemented against sprint acceptance scope, including real quiz-gated progression delivered with Sprint 3.
conclusion.sprint4: Planned: personal performance pages, faculty gradebook, cohort filtering and exports.
conclusion.sprint5: Planned: searchable global lesson directory and persistent audit/telemetry dashboards.

findings: API accepted truthy non-boolean consent; profile enums were not enforced.
implementation: Literal boolean consent and academic profile validation; scroll-gated terms UI retained.

findings: JWT signing secret was evaluated before dotenv initialization and could differ from verification; /auth/me lacked a consistent user id.
implementation: Shared JWT configuration, production secret requirement, password hashing, role guards, and consistent profile identity.

findings: Role-count based seeding could skip the named demo accounts when another account existed.
implementation: Demo accounts are checked by email; seeding remains idempotent; demo module quizzes are backfilled.

findings: Catalog required login; API did not restrict year level to the specified values.
implementation: Guest catalog UI and public subject listing; normalized unique codes and year validation.

findings: Lecture markup displayed as plain text; static upload URLs bypassed learning-path access checks.
implementation: Safe Markdown rendering, faculty-owned authoring, 25 MB attachments, authenticated prerequisite-aware downloads and module detail endpoint.

findings: Direct completion endpoint unlocked modules without assessment; locked lecture text was still delivered to students.
implementation: Passing submissions and designated quiz bindings verify completion flags; locked content is omitted; direct completion requires an actual pass; legacy unverified flags cannot unlock modules.
Existing executive-summary card retained in the module reader.

findings: No quiz studio or student countdown UI; timer validation accepted invalid zero via a default.
implementation: 10-20 minute constraints, circular countdown, final-two-minute warning, automatic submission, server expiry and original deadline on resume.

findings: No manual builder, file parser, import preview, or lecture-file extraction UI.
implementation: Manual question editor; JSON/CSV/Aiken bank uploads and editable previews; text/file lecture generation.

findings: No student quiz UI, no attempt validation, leaked answer keys, and rounded scoring could promote scores below 75%.
implementation: Interactive taker, server grading with exact 75% threshold, idempotent persisted submission, answer-key privacy, own submission history.

findings: Generator used generic unrelated distractors and accepted only pasted content.
implementation: Heuristic definition extraction with lecture-derived distractors; TXT/MD/PDF/DOCX/PPTX support and faculty review.
Strict 4-100 question schema, exactly four distinct options, integer answer-key bounds, indexed errors, syntax linting, quoted CSV parsing, templates and randomized attempt question order.

findings: Client blur/time values could be fabricated and no session deadline or concurrency lock existed.
implementation: Persisted server-owned sessions, unique active-session index, token validation, saved drafts, deduplicated focus warnings, expiry sweep, interrupted-save lease recovery.
Per-attempt answer-choice shuffling preserves displayed letters across resume and maps responses back to original answer indexes.

findings: Quiz-module binding lacked subject/owner checks, prerequisite checks and a failed-attempt review interval.
implementation: Owned same-subject designated binding, passing-result progression, prerequisite enforcement, immediate module retakes after passing or failing, and reader refresh on results.

decisions.publishedQuizEditing: Immutable in this sprint to preserve in-flight assessment scoring.
decisions.answerChoiceOrder: Shuffled per question on each new attempt; persisted for resumption; mapped to the original answer key for grading. Legacy active attempts keep their original order.

coverage: faculty creates subject/modules, generates a preview, sees import errors, imports and publishes a bank
student resumes original deadline and saved answers, records focus warnings, submits, passes and unlocks next module
public subject catalog and mandatory terms acceptance gate
desktop quiz screens and mobile reader screenshots reviewed

verification.liveAtlas: Not tested; configure a working MONGODB_URI for persistent Atlas storage. Tests use local MongoDB only.

limits: Definition-based heuristic generation requires at least four distinct definitions and faculty review.
Scanned documents need OCR; legacy DOC/PPT must be converted.
Browser focus monitoring is an integrity signal and is not proof of cheating.
Existing MongoDB fallback is ephemeral when Atlas is not configured or unavailable.
Local sprint statuses do not synchronize GitHub issues.
